Los Angeles had a law allowing the police access to hotel registers at any time, without probable cause, without an emergency situation, and without a warrant. The Court found this to be Unconstitutional on its face under the Fourth Amendment.

Justices supporting the Fourth Amendment and striking down the law:

Sotomeyer (writer), Kennedy, Ginsburg, Breyer, Kagan

Justices who would have allowed the law to stand:

Scalia, Roberts, Alito, Thomas

http://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/14pdf/13-1175_2qe4.pdf
Supreme Court narrowly upholds Fourth Amendment for Hotel Registers today, 5-4 decision

The supreme court looks set for a fairly radical change in direction under the next president. It's really peculiar reading the dissenting opinions. They simply argue, using excessive hyperbole, that this could make people safer so it should be allowed with seemingly no regard given to its constitutionality in terms of the 4th amendment. As for the hyperbole Scalia references hotels being used as prisons by criminals. Alito and Thomas go even further. They offer hypotheticals ranging from omniscient knowledge that somebody intends to rape and murder somebody in a hotel room, but in spite of said omniscience the police are unable to locate him without the registry which they for some reason cannot obtain a warrant for. They go along the same lines with another hypothetical of some sort of mass child sex trafficking thing going on a pay by the hour hotel that again can only be stopped by being able to demand to see the hotel registry, without a warrant. Constitutional law decided by hyperbolic hypothetical fear mongering in lieu of the constitution. I think we're in for an interesting ride the next 8 years regardless of what happens.

One of the reasons Scalia and the other four allowed the Ten Commandments to stay up on the "state house" in Texas was -- it had been there a long time.
